Beyond this rule, the correspondence must be read with caution: stackings with identical polarization carry vertical monochromatic photocurrents of opposite sign; the spectra reorganize and even reverse sign at some photon energies along a constant-polarization plateau; and the strongest vertical peak of the entire pathway sits where the polarization crosses zero. The reason is structural: the polarization counts polar interfaces, while the shift current reads their positions. Broadband illumination reads the domain sign; monochromatic photocurrent maps can read the stacking registry. In a sliding ferroelectric, the bulk photovoltaic effect can operate as a stacking spectroscopy.

papers.title: Modeling the contact area and intersurface forces between Pb nanoparticles and suspended graphene
papers.abstract: We perform large-scale atomistic simulations to explore the contact mechanics of Pb nanoparticles (NPs) physisorbed on a suspended graphene sheet at zero external load. The study considers the kinetics of the NPs' relative contact area and the distributions of intersurface atomic force magnitudes acting on the NP during self-assembly from the liquid phase, and the size scaling of these quantities for the solidified NPs. The functional forms of both the repulsive and attractive parts of the normal intersurface force distributions for solidified NPs are size-independent for nanoislands with a linear lateral size larger than about 10 nm (or a surface area-to-volume ratio less than about 1 nm$^{-1}$). To first order, the repulsive tail decays exponentially, while the cutoff power law fits more precisely, especially for the high-probability repulsive forces. In both cases, the decay exponent is around -5 nN$^{-1}$. The exponentially modified Gaussian is the best fit for the attractive part for most NP sizes. The time-averaged relative contact area calculated directly in the simulations shows considerable fluctuations for NPs a few nm in diameter, while converging to approximately 0.44 for larger NPs. Based on fitting the normal-force distributions, we obtain analytical expressions for the relative contact area. Ensemble-averaged relative contact areas for NPs larger than around 10 nm, calculated using the analytical expressions, match the time-averaged MD values within statistical error. Our model is the first step towards developing analytical approximations for quantitative estimates of the relative contact area of Pb NPs adsorbed on suspended graphene.

papers.title: Thermo-electric Response Bound on Fluctuations in Coherent Transport
papers.abstract: We establish an accessible lower bound on current noise in coherent electron transport, expressed in terms of responses to reservoir temperatures and chemical potentials. Derived within the Floquet-Nambu scattering formalism using a Cramér-Rao-type inequality, it holds for arbitrary linear combinations of charge and heat currents in normal terminals, including those of hybrid superconducting systems, under static or periodic driving. The bound is tight in experimentally relevant regimes, notably in quantum point contacts with static or oscillating voltages and normal-superconductor junctions, often providing stronger constraints than thermodynamic uncertainty relations. It can be evaluated via experimentally accessible response coefficients, without inferring entropy production or dynamical activity, and provides useful constraints on the precision of nanoscale thermal and quantum devices.

papers.title: General Transport Signatures of Odd-Parity Magnets: Charge--Spin Selection Rules and Temporal--Spectral Separation
papers.abstract: While even-parity altermagnets are known for spatially separating charge and spin currents via the crystal spin Hall effect, the defining transport counterpart for odd-parity magnets remains to be established. Here, we establish temporal and spectral charge--spin separation as a general transport signature across all spin-splitting classes of collinear and noncollinear odd-parity magnets with unitary spin-flip inversion $\mathcal U=[C_2^\perp\Vert P]$. This symmetry restricts charge responses to odd orders and $z$-polarized spin responses to even orders, independent of microscopic mechanism and without requiring spin conservation. For ac drives that reverse sign after half a period, charge and spin currents exhibit opposite half-period parities, and their spectra contain only odd charge and even spin harmonics. This allows dc spin rectification without a dc charge counterpart, even in longitudinal transport and beyond weak fields. We show that although antiunitary $\mathcal Tτ$ enforces odd-parity bands, it reverses the charge--spin selection of Berry-curvature and Berry-curvature-dipole responses, providing a direct transport fingerprint distinguishing the two protecting symmetries. We verify the selection rules for all linear and second-order transport mechanisms and demonstrate harmonic separation in a minimal odd-parity model, representative Floquet-engineered collinear MnPS$_3$, and the equilibrium noncollinear VCl$_2$ family.

papers.title: Structure and relaxation of long-lived odd-parity modes in two-dimensional Fermi liquids
papers.abstract: In two-dimensional Fermi liquids, odd-parity deformations of the Fermi surface relax anomalously slowly at a rate $\sim T^4$, where $T$ is the temperature. However, the leading-logarithmic prediction for the magnitude of this rate $\sim m^4 \ln m$, where $m$ is an angular harmonic index, exceeds exact-diagonalization results and the $\ln m$ scaling is not observed. We resolve this discrepancy by evaluating the 2D Fermi-liquid collision integral for general regular isotropic potentials to leading order in $T/T_F$, including the nonlogarithmic term beyond the $\ln(T_F/T)$ term. We find that the local temperature modulation of the odd mode, which we call the thermal dressing, suppresses relaxation by collinear scattering, with residual relaxation set by large-angle scattering. Such large-angle processes give corrections of order $\ln m/\ln(T_F/T)$ that are not small and must be resummed. We benchmark our results against exact-diagonalization calculations for constant interactions and find agreement over a range $m^2 T/T_F \lesssim 0.4$, and we provide closed-form results for the slowest odd-mode relaxation rate of a spin-polarized dipolar gas.

papers.title: Minimal chiral $p$-wave superconductor
papers.abstract: Chiral $p$-wave superconductors are among the most intriguing topological phases: their vortices bind Majorana zero modes and their edges carry chiral Majorana modes, yet no material has been unambiguously identified as one. Here, we carry the bottom-up approach of Kitaev chains to two dimensions, proposing a minimal chiral $p$-wave superconductor from a square array of quantum dots coupled via Andreev dots. Rashba spin-orbit coupling in the tunnel barriers provides the $p$-wave winding, and a Zeeman field renders the dots spinless. At a sweet spot, the edge states are confined to the outermost row, so that a chiral thermal conductance and a vortex-bound Majorana zero mode with sub-percent splitting emerge already in $3\times3$ and $5\times5$ arrays. Our setup is realizable with existing InAs and Ge quantum-dot arrays.

papers.title: geodesiq: a Python package for geometric diabatic-adiabatic optimal state transfer
papers.abstract: We introduce the geodesiq Python package, which implements a geometric framework for shaping control pulses that achieve high-fidelity state transfer in multilevel quantum systems. The underlying method combines adiabatic and diabatic control into a single metric, suppressing unwanted excitations while allowing selected diabatic passages. Finding the pulse thereby reduces to solving a single first-order ordinary differential equation. We explain how to use geodesiq and illustrate its use explicitly with Landau-Zener transitions, spin-qubit initialization, adiabatic many-body ground-state preparation, and a diabatic-adiabatic transfer in a four-level system.

papers.title: Exploring the Potential of Ultra-Low-Bit Inference on LLM Accelerators
papers.abstract: Vector quantization (VQ) enables ultra-low-bit compression of large language models (LLMs) by encoding groups of values as compact codebook indexes. However, reconstructing these values for computation requires frequent codebook lookups, which conflict with the dataflows of conventional LLM accelerators and limit the performance gains from VQ compression. Consequently, prior work has resorted to VQ-specific accelerator designs, which either incur substantial additional hardware overhead or support only a limited range of inference scenarios. In this work, we argue that existing systolic-array-based LLM accelerators already possess the essential hardware resources for efficient VQ inference, but lack the mechanisms to effectively exploit them. To bridge this gap, we present VQACC, an architectural enhancement that jointly redesigns the existing operand buffer's access logic and data mapping to reuse its storage and port resources for codebook lookups, seamlessly integrating dequantization into the normal operand-addressing dataflow. Evaluation shows that VQACC achieves a 2.63$\times$ speedup over the EVA baseline, with additional hardware occupying only 0.17\% of the compute array's area.

papers.title: FOREST: Coordinating Tree-based HBF, RRAM, and HBM for Efficient Speculative LLM Inference
papers.abstract: Speculative decoding (SD) accelerates large language model (LLM) inference by combining lightweight drafting with parallel target-model verification. However, its stages impose distinct resource demands: target verification requires high-throughput access to large weight sets, sequential drafting executes a compact model under tight latency constraints, and long-context attention processes growing key-value (KV) caches. Conventional GPU-centric SD systems serve these workloads through shared HBM-centric memory and general-purpose compute, creating mismatches in capacity, bandwidth, and computation. These mismatches constrain deployable model-context configurations and limit the efficiency of bandwidth-bound and latency-sensitive operations. We propose FOREST, a heterogeneous memory-centric architecture coordinating HBF, 3D-stacked RRAM, and HBM memory-compute trees for efficient SD. It features: (1) compute-aligned 3D RRAM, combining ultra-wide, low-frequency reads with clock-decoupled interfaces and overlapped SRAM-DCIM weight refills for latency-sensitive drafting; (2) cross-tree numerical co-design, moving block-scaled Q/K/V preprocessing to HBF and RRAM root plates and enabling block-floating-point (BFP) attention with pipelined softmax reduction in the HBM tree; and (3) HBF-aware SD design-space exploration, revealing how bandwidth-compute provisioning and model scale determine performance, energy, and cost trade-offs. Evaluated across six SD configurations spanning 32B-405B target models, FOREST achieves up to 5.5x end-to-end speedup, 11.46x higher decode throughput, and 16.5x higher decode energy efficiency over NVIDIA A800 GPU-based SD baselines. Under a modeled total cost of ownership, FOREST delivers up to 6.73x higher token-generation cost efficiency.

papers.title: Can Language Models See the Circuit in Pixelated RFIC Passives?
papers.abstract: The emergence of inverse-designed, pixelated passives for microwave and millimeter-wave applications has been a major development in the field of RFIC design. These devices, which appear to be QR-code-like in structure, exist in a generalizable, high-dimensional design space that includes conventional passive topologies. However, these structures are naturally unintuitive for designers, and failures or deviations in performance are difficult to debug. In this work, we ask whether a frontier language model can understand, predict, and edit the responses and layout structure of pixelated passives. The agent, run with all tools disabled, is first asked to read layouts on 18x18 and 27x27 tile grids and, in a single reply, predict the input impedance and loss of the structure from 20-100 GHz. On eight GA-synthesized layouts and five random fills, the predicted Smith-chart locus follows full-wave simulation results closely, with a systematic shift that places features about 16% lower in frequency than EM. On multipath loop structures it identifies notches successfully but shows a smaller frequency bias, about half that of an ideal transmission-line model that ignores bends. The agent is then asked to debug seven designs that fail their specification, and given a budget of five EM simulations and at most twelve changed tiles, it is able to improve all seven and bring five designs within specification. These experiments suggest language models can serve as an interpretability and debugging tool for traditionally non-intuitive inverse-designed passives.
